turns.answer_text:
I compared nonlinear regression models using shuffled 5-fold cross-validation. CatBoost performed best, with a validation RMSE of approximately **128 MPa**.

The training data favor lower tempering temperatures for comparable chromium steels. For example, a 13% Cr, 0.12% C sample tempered at 250°C reached **930 MPa**, versus **780 MPa** at 540°C. The selected candidates all avoid the much higher tempering temperatures and prolonged thermal exposures found in many other pool candidates.

| Rank | Candidate | Predicted yield strength |
|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | c006 | ≈955 MPa |
| 2 | c017 | ≈952 MPa |
| 3 | c021 | ≈952 MPa |
| 4 | c031 | ≈945 MPa |
| 5 | c014 | ≈812 MPa |

The first four consistently ranked highly across the tree-based models. Their precise order is uncertain because the prediction differences are small relative to validation error; fifth place is also less secure.

Final: c006, c017, c021, c031, c014

import os
os.environ['OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS']='1'
import numpy as np,pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import KFold,cross_val_predict
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error,mean_absolute_error,r2_score
from sklearn.ensemble import ExtraTreesRegressor,RandomForestRegressor,GradientBoostingRegressor,HistGradientBoostingRegressor
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.svm import SVR
from catboost import CatBoostRegressor
tr=pd.read_csv('/work/b3_htsteel_process_train.csv'); po=pd.read_csv('/work/b3_htsteel_process_pool.csv')
x=tr.drop(columns='target'); x=x.loc[:,x.nunique()>1]; p=po[x.columns];y=tr.target
cv=KFold(5,shuffle=True,random_state=42)
local=(tr.Cr.between(10,14)&(tr.Ni<3)).values
models={
 'cat4':CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1600,depth=4,learning_rate=.035,l2_leaf_reg=4,verbose=False,thread_count=3,allow_writing_files=False),
 'cat5':CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1800,depth=5,learning_rate=.035,l2_leaf_reg=4,verbose=False,thread_count=3,allow_writing_files=False),
 'cat6':CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1800,depth=6,learning_rate=.035,l2_leaf_reg=3,verbose=False,thread_count=3,allow_writing_files=False),
 'cat7':CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1800,depth=7,learning_rate=.035,l2_leaf_reg=3,verbose=False,thread_count=3,allow_writing_files=False),
 'et':ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=700,max_features=1.,min_samples_leaf=1,random_state=42,n_jobs=3),
 'et07':ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=700,max_features=.7,min_samples_leaf=1,random_state=42,n_jobs=3),
 'rf':RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=700,max_features=.8,min_samples_leaf=1,random_state=42,n_jobs=3),
 'gb':GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=700,max_depth=2,learning_rate=.03,min_samples_leaf=3,loss='huber',random_state=42),
 'gb3':GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=700,max_depth=3,learning_rate=.03,min_samples_leaf=3,random_state=42),
 'svr':make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),SVR(C=500,gamma=.025,epsilon=30)),
 'svr01':make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),SVR(C=1000,gamma=.01,epsilon=20)),
}
res=pd.DataFrame({'candidate_id':po.candidate_id})
for name,m in models.items():
 pred=cross_val_predict(m,x,y,cv=cv,n_jobs=1)
 print(name,'RMSE',round(mean_squared_error(y,pred)**.5,1),'MAE',round(mean_absolute_error(y,pred),1),'localRMSE',round(mean_squared_error(y[local],pred[local])**.5,1),'localMAE',round(mean_absolute_error(y[local],pred[local]),1),flush=True)
 m.fit(x,y);res[name]=m.predict(p)
 print(res[['candidate_id',name]].sort_values(name,ascending=False).head(12).to_string(index=False),flush=True)
 if name=='cat5': print('IMPORTANCES',pd.Series(m.feature_importances_,index=x.columns).sort_values(ascending=False).head(15).to_string(),flush=True)
res.to_csv('/tmp/steel_predictions.csv',index=False)
print(res.to_string(index=False),flush=True)

 'cat3':CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1000,depth=3,learning_rate=.035,l2_leaf_reg=3,verbose=False,thread_count=3,allow_writing_files=False),

 'gprbf':make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),GaussianProcessRegressor(kernel=ConstantKernel(1,(.01,100))*RBF(np.ones(len(features)),(.1,100))+WhiteKernel(.05,(.0001,1)),normalize_y=True,n_restarts_optimizer=3,random_state=42)),
 'gpMat':make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),GaussianProcessRegressor(kernel=ConstantKernel(1,(.01,100))*Matern(np.ones(len(features)),(.1,100),nu=1.5)+WhiteKernel(.05,(.0001,1)),normalize_y=True,n_restarts_optimizer=3,random_state=42)),
}
res=pd.DataFrame({'candidate_id':po.candidate_id}); oof=pd.DataFrame({'target':y})
for name,m in models.items():
 x,p=(transform(tr),transform(po)) if name.startswith('gp') else (xx,pp)
 pred=cross_val_predict(m,x,y,cv=cv,n_jobs=1); oof[name]=pred
 print(name,'RMSE',round(mean_squared_error(y,pred)**.5,1),'MAE',round(mean_absolute_error(y,pred),1),'Cr13 RMSE',round(mean_squared_error(y[local],pred[local])**.5,1),'Cr13 MAE',round(mean_absolute_error(y[local],pred[local]),1),'lowtemp RMSE',round(mean_squared_error(y[lowtemp],pred[lowtemp])**.5,1),flush=True)
 m.fit(x,y);res[name]=m.predict(p)
 if name.startswith('gp'): print(m.steps[-1][1].kernel_,flush=True)
 print(res[['candidate_id',name]].sort_values(name,ascending=False).head(10).to_string(index=False),flush=True)
res.to_csv('/tmp/steel_predictions_local.csv',index=False)
print('\nLOCAL OOF\n',pd.concat([tr[['Cr','C','Heat treatment step 2 temperature']],oof],axis=1)[local|lowtemp].round(0).to_string(index=False),flush=True)

import warnings
from sklearn.gaussian_process import GaussianProcessRegressor
from sklearn.gaussian_process.kernels import ConstantKernel,Matern,RBF,WhiteKernel
from sklearn.base import clone
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
mask=(tr.Cr.between(5,17)&(tr.Ni<3)&(tr['Heat treatment step 2 temperature']<900))
tr=tr[mask].reset_index(drop=True); y=tr.target
local=(tr.Cr==13).values
lowtemp=((tr.Cr.between(10,14))&(tr['Heat treatment step 2 temperature']<650)).values
xx=tr.drop(columns='target'); xx=xx.loc[:,xx.nunique()>1];pp=po[xx.columns]
cv=KFold(5,shuffle=True,random_state=42)
features=['C','Cr','Ni','Mo','Mn','Ti','V','W','Heat treatment step 1 temperature','Heat treatment step 1 time','Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate','Heat treatment step 2 temperature','Heat treatment step 2 time','Thermal exposure temperature','Thermal exposure time']
def transform(df):
 a=df[features].copy()
 for c in a:
  if 'time' in c or 'rate' in c:a[c]=np.log1p(a[c])
 return a
models={
 'cat3':CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1000,depth=3,learning_rate=.035,l2_leaf_reg=3,verbose=False,thread_count=3,allow_writing_files=False),
 'cat4':CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1200,depth=4,learning_rate=.035,l2_leaf_reg=3,verbose=False,thread_count=3,allow_writing_files=False),
 'cat5':CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1500,depth=5,learning_rate=.035,l2_leaf_reg=3,verbose=False,thread_count=3,allow_writing_files=False),
 'cat6':CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1500,depth=6,learning_rate=.035,l2_leaf_reg=3,verbose=False,thread_count=3,allow_writing_files=False),
 'et':ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=700,max_features=1.,min_samples_leaf=1,random_state=42,n_jobs=3),
 'rf':RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=700,max_features=1.,min_samples_leaf=1,random_state=42,n_jobs=3),
 'gb':GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=500,max_depth=2,learning_rate=.03,min_samples_leaf=2,random_state=42),
 'gprbf':make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),GaussianProcessRegressor(kernel=ConstantKernel(1,(.01,100))*RBF(np.ones(len(features)),(.1,100))+WhiteKernel(.05,(.0001,1)),normalize_y=True,n_restarts_optimizer=3,random_state=42)),
 'gpMat':make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),GaussianProcessRegressor(kernel=ConstantKernel(1,(.01,100))*Matern(np.ones(len(features)),(.1,100),nu=1.5)+WhiteKernel(.05,(.0001,1)),normalize_y=True,n_restarts_optimizer=3,random_state=42)),
}
res=pd.DataFrame({'candidate_id':po.candidate_id}); oof=pd.DataFrame({'target':y})
for name,m in models.items():
 x,p=(transform(tr),transform(po)) if name.startswith('gp') else (xx,pp)
 pred=cross_val_predict(m,x,y,cv=cv,n_jobs=1); oof[name]=pred
 print(name,'RMSE',round(mean_squared_error(y,pred)**.5,1),'MAE',round(mean_absolute_error(y,pred),1),'Cr13 RMSE',round(mean_squared_error(y[local],pred[local])**.5,1),'Cr13 MAE',round(mean_absolute_error(y[local],pred[local]),1),'lowtemp RMSE',round(mean_squared_error(y[lowtemp],pred[lowtemp])**.5,1),flush=True)
 m.fit(x,y);res[name]=m.predict(p)
 if name.startswith('gp'): print(m.steps[-1][1].kernel_,flush=True)
 print(res[['candidate_id',name]].sort_values(name,ascending=False).head(10).to_string(index=False),flush=True)
res.to_csv('/tmp/steel_predictions_local.csv',index=False)
print('\nLOCAL OOF\n',pd.concat([tr[['Cr','C','Heat treatment step 2 temperature']],oof],axis=1)[local|lowtemp].round(0).to_string(index=False),flush=True)

trace.text:
I compared nonlinear regression models using shuffled 5-fold cross-validation. CatBoost performed best, with a validation RMSE of approximately **128 MPa**.

The training data favor lower tempering temperatures for comparable chromium steels. For example, a 13% Cr, 0.12% C sample tempered at 250°C reached **930 MPa**, versus **780 MPa** at 540°C. The selected candidates all avoid the much higher tempering temperatures and prolonged thermal exposures found in many other pool candidates.

| Rank | Candidate | Predicted yield strength |
|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | c006 | ≈955 MPa |
| 2 | c017 | ≈952 MPa |
| 3 | c021 | ≈952 MPa |
| 4 | c031 | ≈945 MPa |
| 5 | c014 | ≈812 MPa |

The first four consistently ranked highly across the tree-based models. Their precise order is uncertain because the prediction differences are small relative to validation error; fifth place is also less secure.

Final: c006, c017, c021, c031, c014
